nodes.label: Riders
nodes.what: People who hire a bike from a dock.
nodes.how: They use the rider app on a phone.

nodes.label: Operations team
nodes.what: Staff who keep bikes where riders want them.
nodes.how: They plan van routes in the ops console.

nodes.label: Bike share
nodes.what: Everything the city's bike share runs on.
nodes.how: Apps, services and data on one platform. Double-click to go in.

nodes.label: Payment provider
nodes.when: At the end of each ride.
nodes.how: A REST API; the bike share never stores card numbers.

nodes.label: Map tiles
nodes.when: Whenever a rider opens the map.
nodes.how: Tiles over HTTPS, cached on the phone.

nodes.label: City data portal
nodes.how: Receives anonymised trips as CSV.

nodes.label: Rider app
nodes.what: Find a bike, unlock it, pay.
nodes.how: Calls the Trip service and the map tiles.

nodes.label: Ops console
nodes.what: Where the operations team plans the day.
nodes.how: Calls the Fleet service; shows low-battery alerts.

nodes.label: Accounts
nodes.when: At sign-in, and on every call.
nodes.how: Issues tokens that the services check.

nodes.label: Trip service
nodes.how: Prices a ride when it ends and charges it. Its inner view loads when you open it.

nodes.label: Pricing
nodes.what: Works out what a ride costs.
nodes.how: Rules per city zone; v2 adds peak prices.

nodes.label: Fleet service
nodes.how: Reads the telemetry stream and plans rebalancing. Its inner view loads when you open it.

nodes.label: Charging
nodes.how: Not built yet.

nodes.label: Trips database
nodes.how: One row per ride, kept seven years.

nodes.label: Telemetry stream
nodes.how: Partitioned by dock; kept seven days.

nodes.label: Warehouse
nodes.how: Columnar tables; exports anonymised trips weekly.

nodes.label: Docking stations
nodes.how: Report each bike and battery over MQTT; open on command.

nodes.label: Monitoring
nodes.how: Scrapes each service's metrics endpoint.

nodes.label: Status page
nodes.what: Tells riders when something is down.
nodes.how: Updated by hand; nothing calls it yet.

nodes.label: Feature flags
nodes.how: Not wired to the services yet.

nodes.label: Trip API
nodes.how: Validates the token, then hands on.

nodes.label: Unlock coordinator
nodes.how: Sends the dock an open command and waits for its reply.

nodes.label: Trip lifecycle
nodes.how: A state machine; each change is saved and published.

nodes.label: Fare calculator
nodes.what: The price of a finished ride.
nodes.how: Asks Pricing for the rules, then charges the rider.

nodes.label: Trip repository
nodes.how: One table per city.

nodes.label: Event publisher
nodes.what: Tells the rest of the system about rides.
nodes.how: An outbox table drained to the telemetry stream.

nodes.label: Dock listener
nodes.how: Consumes the telemetry stream.

nodes.label: Battery monitor
nodes.how: Raises an alert in the ops console.

nodes.label: Demand forecast
nodes.how: A model trained on a year of trips.

nodes.label: Rebalance planner
nodes.what: Plans where the vans move bikes.
nodes.how: Matches the forecast against stock.

nodes.label: Fleet API
nodes.how: Plans and moves.

nodes.label: Fleet store
nodes.how: A key-value store per dock.

nodes.label: Shoppers
nodes.what: Riders who buy passes, helmets and locks on the site.
nodes.how: They use the storefront in a browser.

nodes.label: Storefront
nodes.when: Whenever a shopper browses or checks out.
nodes.how: A static build served by the edge proxy; it calls the Shop API.

nodes.label: Edge proxy
nodes.how: Serves the storefront and forwards /api to the Shop API.

nodes.label: Shop API
nodes.what: Catalogue of passes and gear, basket, checkout.
nodes.how: Reads and writes the database; puts paid orders on the order queue.

nodes.label: Accounts and sign-in
nodes.what: Who a shopper is, for the shop.
nodes.how: Part of the Shop API; keeps hashed passwords and session tokens apart from the ride accounts.

nodes.label: Database
nodes.how: One schema; nightly backups.

nodes.label: Order queue
nodes.how: A table the worker claims from.

nodes.label: Order worker
nodes.how: Claims an order, books the delivery of gear, activates a pass and sends the confirmation.

nodes.label: Payment provider
nodes.how: The Shop API redirects to it and reads the result. The shop has its own merchant account, apart from ride charges.

nodes.label: Email service
nodes.how: The worker calls its API.

nodes.label: Hosts
nodes.how: One server for the web tier, one for the database.

nodes.label: GitHub
nodes.how: A merge to main builds the image and deploys it to the hosts.

nodes.label: Dashboards
nodes.what: Metrics and logs in one place.
nodes.how: Would read the API's and worker's metrics.

nodes.label: Dock gateway
nodes.how: Takes dock events in and sends settings out.

nodes.label: Dock settings
nodes.what: How long a lock waits, and when a dock raises an alarm.
nodes.when: Changed a few times a year.
nodes.how: A file in the fleet team's repository.

nodes.label: Range check
nodes.what: Drops events a dock's sensors cannot report.
nodes.how: Limits per sensor.

nodes.label: Jump check
nodes.what: Drops a bike seen at two docks at once.
nodes.how: Against the bike's last ten events.

nodes.label: Quarantine
nodes.what: Dock events that failed a check.
nodes.how: A table the fleet team reviews.

nodes.label: Telemetry store
nodes.how: A time-series database.

nodes.label: Weather feed
nodes.how: A national weather service's open API.

nodes.label: Model registry
nodes.what: Every trained demand model, with how far it was off.
nodes.how: Files and a table of scores.

nodes.label: Language model
nodes.how: A hosted model; nothing is kept after the call.

nodes.label: Tone check
nodes.what: Stops drafts that are rude or promise too much.
nodes.how: Rules, then the model as a second reader.

nodes.label: Review
nodes.what: Approves the draft, or hands it to a person.
nodes.how: A refund over 20 goes to the ops console.

nodes.label: Redact
nodes.how: Pattern matching, then a check by the model.

nodes.label: Send
nodes.what: Posts the reply in the rider's help thread.
nodes.how: A push to the rider app.

nodes.label: Help thread
nodes.what: A rider's questions and the replies they got.
nodes.how: One thread per rider.

props.text: The e-bike shall serve as a shared city bike that riders hire from a dock and return to a dock.
The motor shall assist the rider only while the rider is pedalling.
Assistance shall fall away progressively and stop when the bike reaches 25 km/h.
A full charge shall give at least 60 km of assisted riding.
The e-bike shall lock into a dock when it is returned and shall charge while it is docked.
The dock shall lock the e-bike within 2 s of the bike being pushed in.
The battery shall store at least 500 Wh.
Assistance shall follow pedal torque and shall not exceed 250 W of continuous power.
Assistance shall fall away progressively and stop when the bike reaches 25 km/h.
A bike shall last a full day of hires on one charge.

stories.title: A ride, from unlock to payment

steps.caption: Riders hire bikes from Bike share, which charges each ride through a payment provider.
Inside, riders use the rider app, which starts and ends each ride with the trip service.
To unlock a bike, the trip API asks the unlock coordinator, which opens the dock.
When the ride ends, its lifecycle hands it to the fare calculator, which prices it with Pricing's rules.
Last, the fare calculator charges the rider through the payment provider.
